definitions.explanation: Acting on one's own initiative rather than passively following others; taking ownership of one's actions.

examples.japanese: {主体的|しゅたいてき}に{行動|こうどう}する。
{主体的|しゅたいてき}な{学習|がくしゅう}が{大切|たいせつ}だ。
{主体的|しゅたいてき}に{参加|さんか}する{姿勢|しせい}を{持|も}つ。
examples.english: To have an attitude of proactive participation.

notes:
WORD FORMATION:
{主体|しゅたい} (subject, main body) + {的|てき} (adjectival suffix)

EDUCATIONAL CONTEXT:
{主体的|しゅたいてき} is often emphasized in Japanese educational reform, promoting "active learning" where students take initiative rather than passively receiving knowledge.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {主体的|しゅたいてき}に{取|と}り{組|く}む: to engage proactively
- {主体的|しゅたいてき}な{学|まな}び: self-directed learning
- {主体的|しゅたいてき}な{態度|たいど}: proactive attitude

CONTRAST:
- {受動的|じゅどうてき}: passive
- {受|う}け{身|み}: passive
